study_identification_part.si4_title: A multimodal neural signature of face processing in autism within the fusiform gyrus

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To characterize multimodal neural signatures of face processing within the fusiform gyrus in autism by combining normative modeling with linked independent component analysis, and to test whether multimodal components differentiate autistic from non-autistic individuals and relate to social functioning.

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Structured QC and exclusions per modality: structural T1 excluded for excessive motion (N=37), atypicalities (N=21), failed preprocessing (N=3) with CAT/SPM QC metrics; rs-fMRI excluded for incomplete scans (<180 vols, N=8), TR mismatch (N=1), motion (meanFD>0.7mm N=29; maxFD>7.6mm N=38), low coverage (N=24), extreme values (>4 SD, N=12), failed preprocessing (N=1); task-fMRI excluded for high motion (>20% trials with meanFD>0.5mm, N=47); EEG excluded if <20 clean trials (N=9) or <75% channels (N=2); post-exclusion motion/QC differences between groups tested and non-significant.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: "Structural T1-weighted images with excessive head motion (N=37), ... atypicalities (N=21) and failed preprocessing (N=3) were excluded ..."; "Scans with fewer than 180 volumes (N=8) ... meanFD >0.7mm (N=29) and maxFD >7.6mm (N=38) ... low full-brain coverage (N=24), extreme values (>4SD, N=12) and failed preprocessing (N=1) were excluded"; "Hariri task-fMRI datasets with excessive head motion (>20% of trials with a meanFD greater than 0.5mm; N=47) were excluded."; "fewer than 20 clean trials (N=9) or fewer than 75% of channels (N=2)"

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Two-sample t-tests with FDR correction on IC subject loadings for group differences; linear SVM classification with 10-fold CV and AUC comparison between multimodal vs unimodal features; canonical correlation analysis (CCA) with permutation testing (10,000 iterations) relating multimodal ICs to social and nonsocial clinical/cognitive measures; additional tests of extreme deviation counts (|Z|>2.6) via two-sample t-test.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: One multimodal component (IC44) significantly differentiated autistic vs NAI; multimodal components outperformed unimodal in classification; in autism, multimodal components associated with social (but not nonsocial) functioning.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: IC44 showed higher loadings in autism (t = 3.5, P_FDR = 0.027), with contributions primarily from rs-fMRI (R 48.5%, L 35.0%), EEG (L 11.6%), and task-fMRI (R 3.3%), and minor structure contributions (R 1.0%, L 0.5%); hemispheric contributions were similar (R 52.8%, L 47.2%). Multimodal components yielded higher AUC than unimodal under 10-fold CV; CCA links multimodal ICs to social-communicative measures, not nonsocial features.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Analyses restricted to right/left FFG ROIs; eight modality-hemisphere features; 50-component LICA; SVM classification compared multimodal vs unimodal features; clinical data imputed (Extra Trees) to avoid sample loss; task-fMRI values imputed within FFG ROI to match rs-fMRI coverage; group balance and site effects assessed; no external dataset validation.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Normative models were trained across all individuals (autistic and NAI) with site and sex covariates under 10-fold CV rather than using only controls as a reference; ROI confined to FFG; multiple QC thresholds applied per modality; software stack detailed in Supplementary Methods.
